judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic claims are all confirmed: 2/5 < 3/4, 3/4 = 9/12, 2/3 = 16/24 > 15/24 = 5/8, 4/9 < 5/6 across the half benchmark, 7/10 = 28/40, 5/6 = 15/18 > 14/18 = 7/9, 1/2 < 3/5 < 7/10, 7/8 < 9/10, 11/15 = 44/60 < 45/60 = 3/4, and 3/4 > 2/3 > 5/8 > 7/12. The 'extraction warning' the judge worked around is only pdftotext flattening \frac; there really are ten problems. Three findings the judge did not report: (1) the Quick Answers bank prints '---' for problems 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 - six of ten, every comparison relation - so on a sheet whose subject is comparison the fast-grading column is more than half empty even though all six relations are machine-verified; (2) problem 10 asks the student both to order four fractions and to 'name the hiker who walked the farthest', and verify.json id 10 covers only the ordering (the key names Nia in prose but the boxed answer and the verify entry are the ordering alone); (3) rendering page 1 shows problem 1's comparison group broken across a line - '2/5' is stranded at the right margin and the next line opens with the bare rule followed by '3/4.', so the blank is separated from its left operand. The judge scored visual_and_print_quality 4/4.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 (7/8 versus 9/10) is the sharpest item: neither the half benchmark nor rounding to 1 settles it, so the stem directs the student to compare how far each is from a full tank, and the key gives both that route ('with the same numerator, the larger denominator is the smaller amount') and a common-denominator cross-check at 35/40 versus 36/40.

The benchmark number line at the top of the sheet is deliberately value-free and says so: 'No problem's numbers are shown here - use the numbers given in each problem.' It is a reusable reference rather than a solved example.

The key's grading note on problem 10 - 'accept any correct common denominator (a student who uses 48 or 72 gets the same order). The order is what is being assessed' - separates the assessed skill from an incidental choice.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies every string expected; sympify('<') and sympify('>') raise SympifyError and fall through to '---', the placeholder the module reserves for manual-only ids. On a comparison worksheet this silently empties most of the bank.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-123/answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '---' for problems 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9

evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-123/verify.json ids 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 all declare a relation expected of '<' or '>' and all six pass ('10 passed, 0 failed, 0 manual' in gate_log.txt)
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(): the str branch returns '---' on SympifyError

root_causes.description: The verify JSON is authored one entry per problem id rather than one entry per printed response, so a stem that asks for two things is recorded as fully machine verified when only its last component was checked. Nothing in the gate chain compares the number of answer locations the sheet prints against the number of entries covering them.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-123/worksheet.pdf problem 10: 'Order the four fractions from greatest to least, and name the hiker who walked the farthest.'
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-123/verify.json id 10 is a single compare entry with order 'desc' and no entry naming Nia
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-123/answer_key.pdf problem 10 mentions Nia only in the running prose; the boxed answer is the ordering

root_causes.description: A fill-in comparison is written straight into the stem as '$a$ \rule{1cm}{0.4pt} $b$' with nothing holding the three pieces together, so TeX may break the line between them. The preamble offers no comparison macro, and the layout gate only checks overfull boxes, so a split comparison is invisible to every gate.
evidence: Rendering worksheet.pdf page 1 at 100 dpi shows '2/5' alone at the right edge of the second line of the stem and the rule plus '3/4.' opening the third line
gate_log.txt reports the compile clean with no overfull box above 2.0pt, so no existing gate sees the split

improvements.title: Stop pushing relation symbols and interval keywords through sympify in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: render_quick_answers._fmt calls sympy.sympify on every string 'expected' and renders whatever comes back. Two vocabularies are not expressions and must be handled before that call. First, relation strings ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=') from compare problems raise SympifyError and degrade to the '---' the module documents as meaning 'manual, see solution', so a verified answer is advertised as unavailable. Second, the endpoint and closure triple of an inequality problem contains the literal 'open', which sympify resolves to the Python builtin open() and sympy.latex renders as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. Render relations verbatim as math, render an inequality triple as the solution the student writes (x < -3) or as standard interval notation, never sympify the literals open/closed/oo/-oo, and make a sympify result that is not a SymPy object a hard error rather than a rendered repr.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py, build a bank from a verify JSON with six relation-type compare entries expecting '<' or '>' and assert that no bank entry equals '---' and that '$<$' and '$>$' both appear. On today's _fmt every one of the six renders '---', so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading bank stops printing Python internals into a teacher-facing PDF and stops blanking out every comparison answer on comparison-heavy sheets, where today it can be more than half empty.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one formatting helper, and the fixture-locked invariant that bank entries stay plain text outside \ans and \boxed is untouched.

improvements.title: Verify every response the worksheet prints a slot for, not only the final numeric result
improvements.proposed_change: Require one verify-JSON entry (machine or manual) per distinct response the sheet asks the student to write, not one per problem id. That covers each lettered sub-part, the remainder half of a 'quotient with a remainder' answer, the person or option a stem asks the learner to name, and every intermediate form a stem explicitly requests before the final one. Enforce it with a gate that counts printed answer locations per problem in the worksheet tex (\ansline, \ansblank, \answerline, and (a)/(b)/(c) part markers inside a \problem stem) and fails the build when a problem's combined machine plus manual entries cover fewer slots than the sheet prints.
improvements.regression_test: Extend the slot gate fixture with curr-123 problem 10: a stem asking for an ordering AND a name, backed by a single compare entry. The gate must report one uncovered response; adding a second entry (or a manual entry) for the named hiker must clear it.
improvements.expected_impact: Every printed blank has a checked value behind it, so neither the Quick Answers bank nor a boxed key answer can be a partial answer to the question actually asked.
improvements.risk: Counting slots from tex is heuristic and a stem that prints '(a)' as ordinary prose could raise a false failure. Scope the counter to part markers at the start of a sentence and allow an explicit per-problem slot-count override in the verify JSON.

improvements.title: Keep an inline 'a ____ b' comparison group on a single line
improvements.proposed_change: Add a \compareblank{left}{right} macro to templates/worksheet-preamble.tex that wraps the left operand, the rule and the right operand in one unbreakable \mbox, and document it in references/latex-templates.md as the required way to print a fill-in comparison. The raw '$a$ \rule{1cm}{0.4pt} $b$' used today can break anywhere, stranding one operand at the right margin and starting the next line with a bare rule.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/check_layout.py that compiles a stem placing a comparison group near the right margin (the exact prose of curr-123 problem 1) and asserts, via pdftotext -bbox, that the left operand, the rule and the right operand share one baseline. It fails on the raw rule construction used today and passes with \compareblank.
improvements.expected_impact: A child filling in < or > always sees both numbers and the blank as one visual unit on every sheet, instead of depending on where the line happens to break.
improvements.risk: An unbreakable box near the right margin can produce an overfull line, but the layout gate already fails on overfull boxes above 2.0pt so a regression surfaces at build time.

case_summary: Mathematically flawless: all ten comparisons, equivalences and orderings check out, every context states its whole explicitly as the representations-and-applications prompt requires, and the method mix (benchmark, common denominator, equivalent fraction, ordering a set) forces real method choice rather than repetition. The problems are the strong part; the presentation is where it loses ground. Six of the ten Quick Answers entries are em dashes because every comparison relation fails to sympify, problem 10's second requested response (the hiker's name) has no verify entry, and problem 1's fill-in comparison breaks across a line so the blank is separated from the fraction it compares.
